brief_description: Novaterra builds a multilingual enterprise search layer for regulated European customers (finance + pharma). Looking to replace mixed BM25 pipelines with dense+rerank to improve cross-language recall.
latency_targets: p95 < 200ms (EU region); aspirational p95 150ms for single-turn queries; rerank step allowed up to 300ms for high-precision flows
throughput_targets: 500-700 qps sustained; burst 2k qps for quarterly reporting windows
index_scale: Target index ~120M documents (~1.6B tokens). Expect ~1.2-1.6TB raw vectors (1536 dim). Plan sharded HNSW with lightweight quantization for storage savings.
cost_sensitivity: high; internal target < $0.003 per query average across hybrid pipeline; willingness to pay more for EU-resident private deployment with SLA
reranking_strategy: Two-stage retrieval: sparse (BM25) + dense (ANN) -> candidate set 100 -> cross-encoder reranker per-language. Consider per-language rerank models to improve precision@1.
per_language_requirements: DE: recall@10 >= 0.75, focus on compound tokenization
AR/ZH: tolerance for lower recall initially; plan language-specific tokenizers and stopword lists
eval_plan: Build labeled eval sets per language (goal 5k queries total across languages)
A/B test BM25+dense vs dense-only retrieval
Measure MRR, recall@10, precision@1 per language
Latency tests with 128-token contexts and 1k QPS stress runs
poc_scope: 90-day POC: ingest 10M documents (mixed PDFs, HTML, transcripts)
deliver evaluation harness with per-language metrics and dashboard
cost model report and suggested quantization/batching configs
canary on Dedicated in EU region with VPC connectivity

AE note: strong bias toward private/VPC due to regulator guidance
SE: recommend hybrid index (HNSW + IVF+PQ fallback) to balance recall and space
